# {leaf.magic} - Use Modern Icon Libraries in Leaflet Markers

The goal of [leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/) is
to overcome the somewhat outdated “Font Awesome” implementation in
vanilla R [leaflet](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/) by constructing
markers on the fly using
[fontawesome](https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome) or
[bsicons](https://github.com/rstudio/bsicons) and
[magick](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/). There are three issues
[leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/) sets out to
overcome:

- [`leaflet::awesomeIcons()`](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/reference/awesomeIcons.html)
  is limited to Font Awesome 4 👎

- [`leaflet::awesomeIcons()`](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/reference/awesomeIcons.html)
  is limited to a handful of discrete colours 👎

- [`leaflet::awesomeIcons()`](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/reference/awesomeIcons.html)
  is limited to a single marker size 👎

- Vanilla [leaflet](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/) doesn’t provide
  any additional features to construct legends, icon palettes, or such
  like 👎

[leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/) attempts to
solve all of this:

- [`magicIcons()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/magicIcons.md)
  uses up-to-date versions of Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Lucide, and
  Ionicons Icons, powered by
  [fontawesome](https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome),
  [bsicons](https://github.com/rstudio/bsicons) and
  [lucidr](https://github.com/hyperverse-r/lucidr) ✅

- [`magicIcons()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/magicIcons.md)
  uses [fontawesome](https://github.com/rstudio/fontawesome) to grab a
  marker shape, and can therefore colour and resize it however the user
  desires ✅

- [leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/) exports
  functions like
  [`iconBin()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/icon-scales.md)
  and
  [`addIconLegend()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/addIconLegend.md)
  to help developers communicate the meanings of icons to users ✅

[leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/) is thoroughly
documented on the [package
website](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/), which includes a
[getting started
guide](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/articles/leaf-magic.html).

## Installation

You can install the development version of
[leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/) like so:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jack-davison/leaf.magic")
```

![A screenshot of a map produced using the {leaf.magic} R
package.](reference/figures/webshot.png)

A screenshot of a map produced using the {leaf.magic} R package.

# Package index

## Data

In-built data to demonstrate functions.

- [`port_talbot`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/port_talbot.md)
  : Air Quality Monitoring in Neath Port Talbot, 2024

## Icons

Use up-to-date icon libraries in
[leaflet](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/) maps.

- [`magicIcons()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/magicIcons.md)
  : Create a set of Font Awesome, Bootstrap or Ionicons Markers
- [`addIconLegend()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/addIconLegend.md)
  : Add an Icon legend to a map
- [`iconFactor()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/icon-scales.md)
  [`iconBin()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/icon-scales.md)
  [`iconQuantile()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/icon-scales.md)
  : Icon Mapping

## Utilities

Other useful objects exported by
[leaf.magic](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/).

- [`awesomePalette`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/awesomePalette.md)
  :

  Palette used by
  [`leaflet::awesomeIcons()`](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/reference/awesomeIcons.html)

- [`addIconAttribution()`](https://jack-davison.github.io/leaf.magic/reference/addIconAttribution.md)
  : Conveniently add Icon Attributions to a Leaflet Map
